question.text: Chapter V of the SEBI (Intermediaries) Regulations 2008 empowers SEBI, after due process, to impose against a defaulting intermediary (which may include a SIAO employing SIAs) which of the following penalties?

answer.text: Only monetary penalty - no right of suspension, cancellation or warning.
Only cancellation of certificate - intermediaries cannot be warned or suspended.
Warning, censure, prohibition from taking up new assignments, suspension of certificate, cancellation of certificate, or monetary penalty - depending on gravity.
Only criminal prosecution - SEBI has no administrative penalty power against intermediaries.

explanation.text: The Logic: SEBI (Intermediaries) Regulations 2008 Chapter V provides a graded penalty framework: warning / censure for minor defaults, prohibition from taking up new clients or assignments, suspension of the certificate of registration, cancellation of the certificate, or fine / monetary penalty. The sanction chosen is proportionate to the gravity and recurrence of the default. The Trap: Each wrong option narrows the spectrum absurdly. Candidates expecting only one sanction type fail to grasp the graded, proportional nature of the regime. Cross-Exam Context: III-A/III-C and XV RA both test Chapter V graded sanctions. XXIII applies the same regime to SIAOs and their empanelled SIAs. Assessor's Pro-Tip: When reading a SEBI order against any intermediary, map the sanction back to the offence severity matrix: first-time minor -> warning / censure; repeat / material harm -> suspension; willful / fraudulent -> cancellation + monetary penalty. This calibration is useful when advising a SIAO on self-reporting strategy.
